## Symptom

`_metered_spend` in `infra/terraform/bedrock-spend-cap/handler.py` (around line 283) accumulates
token series across all configured regions, but returns `None` as soon as the first region's
`list_metrics`/`get_metric_data` raises `ClientError`. Totals already collected from regions
polled earlier in the loop are discarded.

## Why this matters

The return value is the handler's fast telemetry signal. `None` is interpreted as
`metered_status = "unavailable"`, which sets `signal_unavailable = True`. So a single unhealthy
region converts a partially-successful poll into a declared full metering outage, even when most
regions reported cleanly and the accumulated total is a usable lower bound.

The effect is the same class of defect as the Cost Explorer one fixed on `8d27-d715-0611-48e3`:
a transient fault in one input discards evidence the handler already holds, and the handler then
reports less confidence than it actually has.

## Source

Raised as an advisory finding by the review bot on Gerrit change 2984, patchset 7. Deliberately
left unactioned there to keep that change's scope from growing again after four `LLM-Review -1`
rounds.

## Suggested direction, not yet decided

Distinguish "no region reported" from "some regions reported and at least one failed". The first
is genuinely unavailable; the second is a degraded-but-usable total. Whether a partial total may
be treated as authoritative for enforcement is a judgement call about fail-closed behaviour and
should be settled before implementing — a lower bound that under-reports is safe for *attaching*
the cap but not for *releasing* it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A test proves that when one region raises `ClientError` and another returns token series,
      the accumulated total from the healthy region is returned rather than `None`. Verified by
      that test failing against the current implementation first.
- [ ] A test proves that when every region fails, the function still returns `None`. Verified by
      that test passing.
- [ ] The decision on whether a partial total may drive release as well as attachment is recorded
      on this ticket before the implementation lands. Verified by reading the ticket.
- [ ] Branch coverage over `handler.py` remains at 100%. Verified by a coverage run over
      `infra/terraform/bedrock-spend-cap` reporting 0 missing and 0 partial.
compiled_state.title: Bedrock spend cap: one region's ClientError discards token totals already collected from healthy regions
